rules.check: Each changed fix is implemented in the component that creates the problem rather than compensated for by a caller or presentation layer.
Generic reusable code belongs in `omni.flux.*`, while Remix-specific code belongs in `lightspeed.trex.*`.
Each changed normal control-flow path produces its intended state.
Each changed error, invalid-input, or boundary path preserves correct behavior.
Each changed cancellation, re-entry, or teardown path leaves correct state.
Each changed type, ownership relation, or optional value matches its runtime contract.
Each changed serialized or public API value preserves its declared contract.
Each changed trust boundary validates untrusted input before use.
Each operation-scoped resource acquired by changed code is released on every exit path.
Each changed exception handler preserves or propagates every failure it cannot handle completely.
Changed UI code is not the source of truth for application state.
Changed production timing, retry, or tolerance behavior fixes the underlying asynchronous or data-flow condition instead of hiding it.
Every changed bypass, fallback, compatibility path, or partial migration has a demonstrated current requirement.

Changed executable implementation prefers deletion and repository reuse, then the standard library, native support, and existing dependencies, before adding the minimum custom mechanism or dependency. When changed code wraps or extends a framework or third-party dependency, check the documented features of that dependency for a built-in equivalent and cite it in the finding.
Each changed executable component has one describable responsibility.
Every changed public method or type is required by a current consumer.
No changed function is 200 or more lines long.
Every added abstraction, extension point, setting, feature flag, allow or deny list, or separate configuration file is required by current behavior or established repository architecture.
Changed code uses direct access or explicit typing instead of `getattr()` or `hasattr()` for repository-owned types.
Each object retained for reuse has cost and lifetime that justify retention.
Changed per-item traversal, lookup, and I/O remain linear without repeated stable collection scans, stage or schema lookups, settings reads, disk access, or network requests.
Changed hot paths do not recreate equivalent in-memory values through repeated construction, conversion, or allocation.
Each changed cache has an explicit invalidation event.

Each changed public API reaches a valid state through one call, and callers do not have to call several methods in a fixed order. A new method does not repeat the purpose of an existing method as a variant; the existing method is extended instead.
Changed repository-owned structured data uses typed models, dataclasses, or enums. It does not use `Any`, string-keyed dicts, positional tuples, or hand-written string serialization for that data.

Changed non-test source modules put behavior and mutable state on a class, not in module-level functions or module-level mutable variables. The exceptions are immutable module constants, module-level functions in utility extensions (`omni.flux.utils.*` and `lightspeed.trex.utils.*`), and the getter of an extension-owned singleton with its instance variable, defined in `extension.py` (`get_comfyui_core_instance`, `omni.flux.stage_manager.factory` `get_instance`). Class-level state on the owning class is valid when it follows an existing pattern, such as the per-context submit tasks `ClassVar` of `SubmitComfyUIJobActionWidgetPlugin`.
